summary: Provides a framework for applying GMPLS and the Path Computation Element architecture to wavelength switched optical networks, examining routing and wavelength assignment. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Fiber carries many colors of light at once. This explains how to plan routes and choose a color for each.

questions: what is routing and wavelength assignment
how do gmpls and pce work together for optical networks
subtitle: How GMPLS and the Path Computation Element can control optical networks that switch individual wavelengths of light.

tldr.problem: Optical networks that switch by wavelength have odd constraints, such as asymmetric switches, signal compatibility and wavelength continuity, that ordinary GMPLS and PCE do not capture.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes the optical building blocks, models them with connectivity matrices and port wavelength restrictions, lays out three ways to split Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA), and lists what GMPLS signaling, GMPLS routing and PCE would need to carry.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational framework that prepares the ground for protocol extensions; it defines no new protocol messages itself.

today: RFC 6163 is an Informational framework, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It sets up the requirements that later GMPLS and PCE work for WSONs builds on.

sections.title: What a WSON Is
sections.content:
A Wavelength Switched Optical Network (WSON) is a WDM-based optical network in which switching is done selectively on the center wavelength of an optical signal. It is built from WDM links, tunable transmitters and receivers, Reconfigurable Optical Add/Drop Multiplexers (ROADMs), wavelength converters and electro-optical elements.

WSONs differ from other GMPLS networks: many nodes are highly asymmetric in what they can switch, signal compatibility may matter, and label assignment can be non-local. To provision an optical path, wavelength continuity and resource availability constraints must be met. Finding such paths is called Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA).

The document is a framework for applying GMPLS (RFC 3945) and the Path Computation Element architecture (RFC 4655) to WSONs. It does not address optical impairments in any depth.
sections.eli5: A fiber carries many colors of light, and each message gets one color. Special boxes steer colors in different directions, so planning a trip takes extra care.

sections.title: The Optical Building Blocks
sections.content:
Links. WDM links run over single-mode fibre in optical bands such as the C-band (1530-1565 nm). ITU-T grids define the channels: the DWDM grid is centered on 193.1 THz with spacings including 12.5, 25, 50 and 100 GHz, and the CWDM grid uses 20 nm steps from 1271 nm to 1611 nm. RFC 6205 gives a label format for these grids.

Transmitters and receivers. Some are fixed to one wavelength, others are tunable. Tuning range and tuning time matter, since thermal tuning may take seconds while electronic tuning can be under a millisecond.

Switching elements. A ROADM is a wavelength-selective switch with line side ports and add/drop tributary ports. Its key feature is highly asymmetric switching: in a degree-2 ROADM, an added signal can only go out the line side. Splitters copy a signal to all outputs, combiners merge inputs into one output, and Fixed Optical Add/Drop Multiplexers (FOADMs) drop a preset wavelength to a fixed port, possibly also continuing it ("drop and continue").

Electro-optical elements. Regenerators come in 1R, 2R and 3R classes, with 3R doing full pulse regeneration with clock recovery. Wavelength converters emit an equivalent signal at a different wavelength, either by optical-electronic-optical (OEO) conversion or optically through non-linear effects.
sections.eli5: Think of colored pipes and special junction boxes. Some boxes can send any color anywhere, some only one color to one place, and some boxes can repaint a color.

sections.title: Modeling the Network for the Control Plane
sections.content:
The core modeling idea is a connectivity matrix Amn, where Amn = 0 or 1 says whether a wavelength on input port m can reach output port n. A ROADM has a sparse, switched matrix, an OXC a dense one, and splitters, combiners and FOADMs have a fixed matrix. Each port also carries wavelength restrictions: for example colored ports (single fixed wavelength) versus colorless ports (single arbitrary wavelength).

Wavelength converter pools are modeled in three stages: an input matrix WI, per-converter input and output wavelength constraints plus a usage-state vector WC, and an output matrix WE. Electro-optical elements are described by input constraints (modulation formats, G-PID, bitrate, FEC, configurability), output constraints, and processing capabilities such as regeneration and wavelength conversion.

A WSON signal is characterized by modulation format, FEC, center frequency, bitrate and G-PID. The first three can change along the path, while bitrate and G-PID cannot.
sections.eli5: Draw a grid listing which door each color can go in and out of. A 1 means the color can pass and a 0 means it cannot.

sections.title: Routing and Wavelength Assignment
sections.content:
With full wavelength conversion at every node, an optical network can be controlled much like an MPLS packet network, with wavelengths assigned hop by hop. Without converters, a path must use a single wavelength free along its whole length. This is the wavelength continuity constraint. With limited or no converters, choosing both links and wavelengths is RWA. The RFC does not pick an algorithm.

It describes three architectural approaches:

  • Combined RWA (R&WA): one entity, either a PCE or the ingress node, does both. It needs detailed, up-to-date network information.
  • Separated R and WA (R+WA): one entity routes and passes one or more paths to a second that assigns the wavelength.
  • Routing and Distributed WA (R+DWA): one entity routes and wavelengths are picked hop by hop through signaling, using Label Sets. It needs less information but may cause higher blocking probability in a heavily loaded network.

A worked example has three routers, eight WSON nodes and 18 links, with four wavelengths WL1 to WL4. A first R1 to R2 path takes WL1, a second takes WL2, and a third request from R2 to R3 then fails because all four possible paths are in use. Rerouting after a failure of L5 can use 3R regeneration at an OEO converter.
sections.eli5: To send a message you need a road and a color. If the color must stay the same the whole way, you have to find a color nobody else is using on every road you take.

sections.title: What GMPLS and PCE Would Need
sections.content:
Signaling. GMPLS already supports the lambda LSP encoding type (value 9) from RFC 3471 and, for G.709, value 13 from RFC 4328. Distributed wavelength assignment can use the Label Set object in RSVP-TE, intersecting available wavelengths hop by hop. GMPLS signaling cannot yet say that a node should regenerate a signal, which shared regenerator pools and reconfigurable regenerators would need.

Routing. RFC 4202 defines the Lambda Switch Capable (LSC) interface descriptor. To characterize a WSON, routing would also need to convey WDM link properties, transmitter ranges, ROADM and FOADM properties and converter properties. Knowing which specific wavelengths are in use is not currently possible with GMPLS routing. With current DWDM systems ranging from 16 to 128 channels, a simple bitmap is feasible.

PCE. RWA can be computationally intensive, and PCEP (RFC 5440) with some enhancement is well positioned to support it, including batch and backup-path requests. The RFC also suggests indicating RWA-capable PCEs through PCE discovery.
sections.eli5: The existing road-planning tools already know some of this, but they need new words so they can talk about colors, repainting stations and which colors are taken.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document does not require changes to the security models of OSPF-TE, RSVP-TE and PCEP. However, satisfying RWA requirements with existing protocols may significantly increase their load, which could make the network more vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks. The extra distributed information also discloses network capabilities that an operator may want to keep private, so securing it should be considered.
sections.eli5: Sharing so much detail about the network makes it busier and tells outsiders more, so it needs extra protection.

items.title: Combined RWA
items.text: One entity, a PCE or the ingress node, computes route and wavelength together.

items.title: Separated R and WA
items.text: A routing entity passes candidate paths to a wavelength assignment entity.

items.title: Routing plus distributed WA
items.text: Route computed first, wavelength chosen hop by hop in signaling.
